record.original_question: Deterministic Pseudospectral Shattering: Give a provably correct and efficient deterministic algorithm for the following task: on input $A C^n x n$ and $delta>0$, output a perturbation $E$ with $ |E | delta$ such that $kappa_eig(A+E) C(delta/n)^c$, where $C,c$ are universal constants. In this context, efficient means $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ arithmetic operations, either in exact arithmetic or, more ambitiously, in finite arithmetic with $O( ^c(n/delta))$ bits of precision.

evidence.quote: Give a provably correct and efficient \emph{deterministic} algorithm for the following task: on input $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ and $\delta>0$, output a perturbation $E$ with $\|E\|\le \delta$ such that $\kappa_{eig}(A+E)\le C(\delta/n)^c$, where $C,c$ are universal constants. In this context, efficient means $O(n^3\log^c(n/\delta))$ arithmetic operations, either in exact arithmetic or, more ambitiously, in finite arithmetic with $O(\log^c(n/\delta))$ bits of precision.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a matrix $M\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ that is diagonalizable as $M=VDV^{-1}$ with $D$ diagonal, define the eigenvector condition number
$$\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(M)=\inf_{V}\,\|V\|\,\|V^{-1}\|,$$
where the infimum is over all such diagonalizations and $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the spectral norm (set $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(M)=\infty$ if $M$ is not diagonalizable).

Construct a deterministic algorithm with the following provable guarantee. There exist universal constants $C,c>0$ such that, given as input any matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with $\|A\|\le 1$ and any parameter $\delta>0$, the algorithm outputs a perturbation $E\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with
$$\|E\|\le\delta\qquad\text{and}\qquad \kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(A+E)\le C\left(\frac{n}{\delta}\right)^{c}.$$
The algorithm must be efficient, in the sense of using $O(n^3\,\log^{c}(n/\delta))$ arithmetic operations, either in exact arithmetic, or—more ambitiously—in finite-precision arithmetic with $O(\log^{c}(n/\delta))$ bits of precision.

Either exhibit such a deterministic algorithm together with a proof of correctness, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing pseudospectral shattering algorithms (Banks–Garza-Vargas–Kulkarni–Srivastava and the generalized/sparse extensions) are randomized: they rely on adding a random Gaussian (or sparse random) perturbation to achieve the eigenvector-conditioning guarantee. Subsequent work through 2024 (generalized pencils, sparse perturbations) still uses randomness, and no deterministic polynomial-time algorithm achieving the stated guarantee appears in the literature, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Pseudospectral Shattering, the Sign Function, and Diagonalization in Nearly Matrix Multiplication Time
status_evidence.snippet: Randomized algorithm using a complex Gaussian perturbation to achieve pseudospectral shattering and diagonalize an arbitrary matrix.
status_evidence.claim: The original shattering algorithm is randomized.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Pseudospectral Shattering and Inverse-Free Matrix Pencil Diagonalization
status_evidence.snippet: Extends shattering to matrix pencils, still relying on random perturbation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extensions remain randomized, no deterministic version reported.

status_evidence.title: Sparse Pseudospectral Shattering
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sparse random perturbations achieving pseudospectral shattering.
status_evidence.claim: Most recent work continues to rely on randomness.
